in_text_mentions: d boy, weighing 32 kg and a known case of ANE1, was scheduled for total hip reconstruction under general anesthesia. The child had been well until four years of age when he tested positive for influenza (H1N1) and later developed H1N1 meningitis. This progressed to acute disseminated encephalomyelitis. An MRI of the brain revealed a hyperintense signal in the external capsules, both thalami, dorsal pons, and hippocampi, with relative sparing of the basal ganglia, suggesting an infective or metabolic encephalopathy (Figure 1). A genetic workup revealed a monoallelic mutation of the RanBP2 gene.
